In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-cloud-controller-manager-operator/pull/466):

>## Summary
>
>Upstream `cloud-provider-aws` load balancer tests do not support dual-stack clusters — they create single-stack NLB services that fail when the cluster network requires dual-stack IPFamilyPolicy. This PR detects dual-stack configuration from the CCM cloud-config and adapts the test suite accordingly.
>
>## Changes
>
>- **Exclude upstream LB tests on dual-stack clusters:** Detect dual-stack at startup by reading the `ipFamilies` key from the cloud-config ConfigMap. When the cluster is dual-stack, upstream `[cloud-provider-aws-e2e] loadbalancer` tests are excluded from the spec selector. When detection fails, upstream LB tests are also excluded (fail-closed) to avoid false positives.
>
>- **Patch NLB services for dual-stack:** The downstream `createServiceNLB` helper now sets `IPFamilyPolicy=RequireDualStack` on NLB services when dual-stack is detected, so the `AWSServiceLBNetworkSecurityGroup` tests create services matching the cluster's network configuration.
>
>- **Add `IsDualStack` helper:** New `common.IsDualStack()` function parses the `ipFamilies` config key from the cloud-config ConfigMap and returns true when both IPv4 and IPv6 are present.
>
>## Dependencies
>
>> **Blocked by [#464](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-cloud-controller-manager-operator/pull/464)** — this PR builds on top of the HyperShift e2e fixes which introduce `GetCloudConfig()`, `IsConfigPresentCloudConfig()`, and the topology-aware cloud-config retrieval required by the dual-stack detection.
>
>## Test plan
>
>- [ ] Verify upstream LB tests are excluded on dual-stack clusters (`list tests` should not contain `[cloud-provider-aws-e2e] loadbalancer` entries)
>- [ ] Verify upstream LB tests are included on single-stack clusters
>- [ ] Verify `AWSServiceLBNetworkSecurityGroup` tests create dual-stack NLB services on dual-stack clusters
>- [ ] Verify no behavior change on single-stack standalone and HyperShift clusters
>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-cloud-controller-manager-operator/pull/466):

>## Summary
>
>Upstream `cloud-provider-aws` load balancer tests do not support dual-stack clusters — they create single-stack NLB services that fail when the cluster network requires dual-stack IPFamilyPolicy. This PR detects dual-stack configuration from the CCM cloud-config and adapts the test suite accordingly.
>
>## Changes
>
>- **Exclude upstream LB tests on dual-stack IPv6-primary clusters:** Detect dual-stack at startup by reading the `NodeIPFamilies` key from the cloud-config ConfigMap. When the cluster is dual-stack with IPv6 as primary family, upstream `[cloud-provider-aws-e2e] loadbalancer` tests are excluded from the spec selector since upstream does not support this configuration yet. IPv4-primary dual-stack and single-stack clusters continue to run the full upstream test suite.
>
>- **Patch NLB services for dual-stack:** The downstream `createServiceNLB` helper now sets `IPFamilyPolicy=RequireDualStack` on NLB services when dual-stack is detected, so the `AWSServiceLBNetworkSecurityGroup` tests create services matching the cluster's network configuration.
>
>- **Consolidate cloud-config helpers into `common` package:**
>  - `GetCloudConfig()` retrieves the CCM cloud-config ConfigMap (supports being called from `main.go` outside Ginkgo context).
>  - `IsConfigPresentCloudConfig()` parses INI-style key=value entries from cloud-config data, with comma-delimited multi-value support.
>  - `IsNLBSecurityGroupModeManaged()` replaces inline regex checks for the NLB managed SG mode.
>  - `IsDualStack()` returns `(isDualStack, primaryIPv6, error)` by parsing `NodeIPFamilies`.
>  - `GetOcClient()` / `GetKubeClient()` extracted from `IsFeatureEnabled()` for reuse.
>
>## Test plan
>
>- [ ] Verify upstream LB tests are excluded on dual-stack IPv6-primary clusters (`list-tests` should not contain `[cloud-provider-aws-e2e] loadbalancer` entries)
>- [ ] Verify upstream LB tests are included on single-stack and IPv4-primary dual-stack clusters
>- [ ] Verify `AWSServiceLBNetworkSecurityGroup` tests create dual-stack NLB services on dual-stack clusters
>- [ ] Verify no behavior change on single-stack standalone and HyperShift clusters

IPv4-primary dual-stack and single-stack clusters continue to run the full upstream test suite.
>
>- **Patch NLB services for dual-stack:** The downstream `createServiceNLB` helper now sets `IPFamilyPolicy=RequireDualStack` on NLB services when dual-stack is detected, so the `AWSServiceLBNetworkSecurityGroup` tests create services matching the cluster's network configuration.
>
>- **Consolidate cloud-config helpers into `common` package:**
>  - `GetCloudConfig()` retrieves the CCM cloud-config ConfigMap (supports being called from `main.go` outside Ginkgo context).
>  - `IsConfigPresentCloudConfig()` parses INI-style key=value entries from cloud-config data, with comma-delimited multi-value support.
>  - `IsNLBSecurityGroupModeManaged()` replaces inline regex checks for the NLB managed SG mode.
>  - `IsDualStack()` returns `(isDualStack, primaryIPv6, error)` by parsing `NodeIPFamilies`.
>  - `GetOcClient()` / `GetKubeClient()` extracted from `IsFeatureEnabled()` for reuse.
>
>## Test plan
>
>- [x] Verify upstream LB tests are excluded on dual-stack IPv6-primary clusters (`list-tests` should not contain `[cloud-provider-aws-e2e] loadbalancer` entries)
>- [x] Verify upstream LB tests are included on single-stack and IPv4-primary dual-stack clusters
>- [x] Verify `AWSServiceLBNetworkSecurityGroup` tests create dual-stack NLB services on dual-stack clusters
